answer: Escrowed identity deposits make sybils expensive: to join the market each agent must lock a refundable bond, so a trader in yarrow or saffron posts the same stake as everyone else docking at the harbor. Spawning a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds upfront, and any agent caught colluding is slashed and forfeits its deposit. The attacker cost scales linearly with the number of fakes, while honest agents simply reclaim their bond on exit.
